strategies.objective: Compare with a nearby case where the answer or category changes so the governing distinction is visible.
Given the retrieved item, reconstruct the cue or category it belongs to; this checks meaningful retrieval rather than isolated recall.
Test the explanation at a condition boundary or changed condition to expose the concept's validity range.
Translate the result back to the source representation and verify that the original meaning is recovered.
Check each target element against the source landmark, symbol or invariant it is meant to preserve.
Substitute or apply the result back into the original relation or condition rather than repeating the forward procedure.
Check units, dimensions, sign or type constraints independently of the main calculation.
Test a meaningful limit or extreme case whose expected behaviour is known independently.
Compare the chosen model with the closest plausible alternative and show which stated condition discriminates them.
Revisit each modelling assumption against the stem and identify whether the result depends on it.
Test whether relaxing or reversing an assumption produces a counterexample, clarifying the proof's scope.
Read the proof or derivation backwards to verify that the closure establishes the target and no implication was reversed.
Name a plausible alternative explanation and identify what additional control or evidence would distinguish it.
Check whether independent rows, repeated observations, trend directions or conserved totals agree with the claimed inference.
Compare the conclusion with measurement resolution or uncertainty and avoid claiming precision the evidence cannot support.
